theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main job of the bell staff (bell attendants)?
options: To check guests in and take their payments at the desk
To handle guests' luggage and run errands for guests
To clean guest rooms and change the bed linen
To cook room service meals for guests in the kitchen

questions.stem: Who usually leads the bell team on a shift and gives out the jobs?
options: The head chef
The night auditor
The bell captain
The pool attendant

questions.stem: Before the shift starts, what should a bell attendant check at the bell desk?
options: That all the guest bills have been printed for the day
That the restaurant tables are laid for breakfast
That the pool towels have been counted and folded
That trolleys, tags and the bell log are ready

questions.stem: Why must bell staff be well groomed, with a clean uniform and a name badge?
options: They are often the first staff guests meet on arrival
Guests choose their room by the look of the bell staff
Bell staff are paid according to how smart they look
The uniform protects them from the heavy luggage

questions.stem: A car with guests stops at the main entrance. What should the bell attendant do first?
options: Wait at the bell desk until the guests come inside
Ask the driver to unload the bags onto the ground
Go to the car, greet the guests and help them out
Call housekeeping to come and collect the luggage

questions.stem: As the guests' luggage is unloaded from the car, what should you check?
options: That none of the bags is heavier than your own
That no bag is left behind in the car
That every bag has a lock fitted to it
That the guests have already tipped the driver

questions.stem: Why do you count the bags with the guest when they arrive?
options: So that the guest can be charged for each bag
So you know how many trips the lift will need
So that you both agree how many bags there are
So that you can choose which bag to carry first

questions.stem: As a suitcase comes out of the taxi, you see its handle is broken. What should you do?
options: Say nothing and carry it carefully to the room
Fix it yourself with tape before the guest sees
Point it out to the guest and note it in the log
Leave it in the lobby for the taxi driver to fix

questions.stem: What is written on the luggage tag for an arriving guest's bag at the bell desk?
options: The guest's credit card number
The guest's home address and phone
The price the guest paid for the room
The guest's name and room number

questions.stem: Guests arrive before their room is ready. What should happen to their luggage?
options: Tag it and lock it in the luggage room for now
Leave it in the lobby so the guests can watch it
Put it in any empty room until theirs is ready
Ask the guests to carry it around with them

questions.stem: Which bags should you take special care with when unloading?
options: Only the bags that look the most expensive
Bags that are marked or said to be fragile
Only the bags that the guest paid extra for
Bags that belong to guests who will tip well

questions.stem: It is raining heavily when guests arrive. What should bell staff do?
options: Wait inside until the rain stops before helping
Ask the guests to unload their own bags quickly
Meet them with an umbrella and cover the luggage
Leave the luggage in the rain and carry the coats

questions.stem: Before you lift a suitcase, what should you do?
options: Lift it in one quick pull to save your energy
Ask the guest to help lift it onto your back
Kick it gently to find out how heavy it is
Tilt it to test the weight, and plan the lift

questions.stem: What is the safe way to move a fully loaded luggage trolley?
options: Pull it behind you while walking backwards fast
Run with it, so that the guest is not kept waiting
Push it at a steady pace, so you can see ahead
Let it roll down ramps by itself to save effort

questions.stem: Where should garment bags (suit and dress bags) go on a bell trolley?
options: Hung on the top rail of the trolley
Folded under the heaviest cases
Rolled up inside a suitcase
Laid flat on the floor of the lift

questions.stem: A guest's trunk is too heavy for you to lift safely. What should you do?
options: Lift it anyway, as that is part of your job
Get a colleague to help, or use a trolley
Drag it across the floor all the way to the room
Ask the guest to carry it while you take the rest

questions.stem: A guest checks out at noon but flies at 6 p.m., and wants to leave her bags. What do you do?
options: Keep them behind the front desk where anyone can see
Tell her the property cannot help after check-out
Put them in a corner of the lobby for her to collect
Tag them, give her the stub and lock them away

questions.stem: What is the claim stub (claim ticket) for?
options: The guest shows it to collect the stored bags
It lets the guest skip the queue at check-in
It shows how much the guest must pay for storage
It is given to the taxi driver for the airport

questions.stem: A man comes to collect stored bags but has lost his claim stub. What should you do?
options: Give him the bags if he can describe the colour
Hand over whatever bags he points to
Check his ID, then follow the procedure
Tell him the bags are now lost for good

questions.stem: Why must the luggage storage room be kept locked?
options: So that the room stays cool for the bags
So that guests cannot rest in there
So that housekeeping can keep linen there
So only bell staff can reach the bags

questions.stem: How should bags be arranged in the luggage storage room?
options: Grouped and tagged by guest, in a set order
Piled on top of each other in one big heap
Mixed together, so no one knows whose they are
Spread out across the floor near the door

questions.stem: A guest asks you to store a bag that has cash and jewellery in it. What should you advise?
options: Store it, and keep the jewellery yourself for safety
Store it, but leave the bag unlocked so you can check
Refuse to store any of the guest's bags at all
Put the valuables in the safe deposit box instead

questions.stem: When stored bags are handed back, what should you write in the bell log?
options: Nothing at all; tear out the page and throw it away
The time, the stub number and who collected them
Nothing, because the bags have now gone
The guest's credit card number, for safety

questions.stem: A guest phones the bell desk for help with luggage at check-out. What should you ask?
options: How much the guest will tip for the help
Why the guest is leaving the property early
The room, how many bags, and when to come
Whether the guest enjoyed the food

questions.stem: You collect a departing guest's bags from the room. What should you check with the guest before you leave the room?
options: That the minibar is still full and untouched
That the bed has been made up neatly
That nothing is left in the drawers or safe
That the TV has been left switched on

questions.stem: Before you load a departing guest's luggage into the car, what should you check with the desk?
options: That the guest has filled in a feedback card
That the room has been cleaned for the next guest
That the driver has a full tank of fuel
That the guest's bill has been settled

questions.stem: Why do you count the bags again with the guest at the car?
options: So the guest can confirm nothing is left behind
So that the driver can charge the guest per bag
So you know how heavy the car will be
So the bags fit in the order you loaded them

questions.stem: How should luggage be loaded into the boot (trunk) of a car?
options: Small bags first at the bottom, heavy cases on top
Heavy cases first at the bottom, small bags on top
Any way at all, as long as the boot will close
Fragile bags at the bottom, with cases on top

questions.stem: After a guest has left, you find their phone charger in the room. What should you do?
options: Keep it, because the guest has gone
Give it to the next guest in the room
Throw it away with the room rubbish
Hand it in to lost property, logged

questions.stem: A guest waiting for the airport shuttle asks you to watch his bags for a few minutes. What should you do?
options: Keep them in sight, or tag and store them
Leave them by the door and carry on with your work
Put them on the shuttle bus before he gets there
Ask another guest to look after them for him

questions.stem: The front desk gives you a parcel for a guest. How should you deliver it?
options: Leave it outside the room door for the guest
Give it to any guest who says that it is theirs
Open it to check that nothing inside is broken
Knock, say who you are and hand it to the guest

questions.stem: Why is an errand card (errand slip) filled in?
options: To show how many tips you received that day
To record each job, its time and who did it
To let guests order meals from the bell desk
To book the guest's dinner in the restaurant

questions.stem: You go to deliver a message and the guest's door has a Do Not Disturb sign. What should you do?
options: Do not knock, and pass the message on another way
Knock loudly until the guest answers the door
Open the door with a master key and leave it inside
Throw the message away, as the guest is busy

questions.stem: A guest asks you to post some letters for them. What should you do?
options: Put them in your pocket and post them next week
Log the errand, post them promptly and tell the guest
Read them first, to make sure the addresses are right
Ask the guest to post them at the airport

questions.stem: The bell desk takes a phone message for a guest. How should it be written?
options: Quickly, on any scrap of paper that is close by
Clearly, with the date, time, caller and message
From memory, once the shift has ended and you have time
In the guest's own language only

questions.stem: A guest asks how to get to Dunn's River Falls. What should you do?
options: Give clear directions and offer licensed transport
Tell them it is too far away and not worth a visit
Flag down any car passing the gate for them
Tell them to follow the other guests

questions.stem: Why should bell staff call only taxis that the property has approved?
options: Because approved taxis are always the cheapest
Because guests are not allowed other transport
Because bell staff are paid by the taxi firms
Because the drivers are licensed and known to be safe

questions.stem: A guest asks you to recommend a restaurant in Ocho Rios. What is the best answer?
options: Recommend only the place your cousin owns
Say you never eat out, so you cannot help them
Suggest a few good places and their hours
Tell them the food outside is never safe

questions.stem: A guest wants to change US$100 into J$. What should you tell them?
options: To change it with you, at your own rate
The front desk or a licensed cambio can help
Jamaica accepts only US$, so there is no need
To change it with a man outside the gate

questions.stem: A guest asks about the weather for a boat trip tomorrow, and you are not sure. What should you do?
options: Tell them it will be fine, so they are not worried
Say that the weather is not part of your job
Tell them it will rain, just to be on the safe side
Check a reliable forecast or ask the tour desk

questions.stem: A bag has been left alone in the lobby for a long time, and no one claims it. What should you do?
options: Open it up to find out who it belongs to
Carry it to the luggage room and forget about it
Leave it untouched and tell security at once
Leave it there, as someone will come back for it

questions.stem: A visitor who is not a guest asks you which room Mr Thompson is in. What should you do?
options: Do not give the room; offer to call him from the desk
Tell them the room number, as they know his name
Take them straight up to the room yourself
Tell them to go and wait outside his room

questions.stem: Someone you do not know asks you to let them into a room because they lost their key. What should you do?
options: Open the door with a master key to help them
Give them a spare key from the bell desk drawer
Send them to the front desk to prove who they are
Ask housekeeping to open it while you watch

questions.stem: A guest hands in a wallet found in the lobby. What should you do?
options: Record it and hand it to lost property or security
Keep it at the bell desk in case the owner returns
Open it and phone the numbers you find inside
Give it to the first person who asks for a wallet

questions.stem: What is the bell log (bell sheet) used for?
options: To write down guests' credit card details
To record each arrival, departure and errand
To list the dishes on the room service menu
To show which members of staff are on leave

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

What is the staff member called who gives guests information and books tours, transport and restaurants?
Which agency runs the Team Jamaica training for people who work with visitors?

essays.stem: Describe the duties of a bell attendant during a busy day shift at a resort.
essays.modelAnswer: At the start of the shift, the bell attendant reports to the bell captain in clean uniform with a name badge and checks the bell desk: trolleys clean and working, luggage tags, claim stubs, the bell log and the storeroom key. Through the day, the attendant greets arriving guests at the entrance, helps them from cars, unloads and counts the luggage, tags it and rooms the guests or delivers the bags. For departures, they collect luggage from rooms when called, check that nothing is left, confirm that the bill is settled and load the luggage into the car. They store and return luggage using claim stubs. They deliver messages, parcels and newspapers, run errands, and give information about the property, local attractions and approved transport. They watch for security problems, such as unattended bags, and hand in lost property. Every job is written in the bell log, and at the end of the shift they hand over to the next team.
markingPoints: Reports for duty well groomed and checks the bell desk equipment
Arrivals: greets, unloads, counts and tags luggage, rooms guests
Departures: collects luggage, checks the room and the bill, loads the car
Stores luggage; delivers messages and parcels; runs errands; gives information
Security awareness, lost property and recording every job in the bell log

essays.stem: Describe how you would receive a family arriving by taxi at the main entrance, and look after their luggage.
essays.modelAnswer: When I see the taxi arrive, I go out at once with a trolley, smile and greet the family with "Welcome to" the property's name. I open the car doors and help the guests out, taking care with children and older people. I unload the luggage from the boot with the driver, lifting safely with bent knees and a straight back. I count the bags with the guests and point out any damage, such as a broken handle, and I check the car so nothing is left behind. I load the trolley with heavy cases at the bottom, fragile bags on top and garment bags on the rail. I lead the family to the front desk for check-in and stay with the luggage, never leaving it alone. When they have checked in, I tag the bags with their name and room number and room them, or deliver the bags if the room is not ready yet, storing them in the locked luggage room with a claim stub.
markingPoints: Goes to the car promptly, greets and helps the guests out
Unloads safely and checks nothing is left in the car
Counts bags with the guests and points out any damage
Loads the trolley correctly and never leaves the luggage alone
Tags bags, then rooms the guests or stores the luggage securely

essays.stem: Explain how you would store a guest's luggage safely for the day and hand it back when they return.
essays.modelAnswer: I count the bags with the guest and ask if there are any valuables or fragile items. I advise the guest to put cash, jewellery, passports and medicines in the safe deposit box or keep them, not in the stored bags. I fill in a two-part claim tag for each bag: one part goes on the bag and the matching stub goes to the guest. I write the guest's name, the number of bags, the stub numbers, the date and time and my name in the luggage storage log. I take the bags to the locked luggage room and place them together, in order, with the tags showing. When the guest returns, I ask for the claim stubs and check they match the tags on the bags and the log. If a stub is lost, I check the guest's ID against the log and follow the supervisor's procedure. I hand over the bags, count them with the guest and write the time and who collected them in the log.
markingPoints: Counts bags and advises that valuables go in the safe deposit box
Two-part claim tag: one part on the bag, stub to the guest
Records the storage in the log
Keeps bags together in the locked luggage room
Returns bags only against the matching stub (or ID and procedure), counts and records

essays.stem: Describe how you would handle a departing guest's luggage, from the phone call to the bell desk until the car leaves.
essays.modelAnswer: When the guest calls, I note the room, the number of bags and the time they want me, and I write it in the bell log. I arrive on time with a clean trolley, knock and announce "Bell service". I greet the guest, count the bags with them and ask if there is anything fragile. I politely remind the guest to check the drawers, wardrobe, bathroom and safe so nothing is left behind. I load the trolley safely and take the luggage to the lobby, keeping it with me. I check with the front desk that the guest has settled the bill before I release the luggage. When the car or shuttle arrives, I count the bags again with the guest and load them into the boot with heavy cases at the bottom. I thank the guest, wish them a safe journey and invite them to come back. Last, I record the departure in the bell log.
markingPoints: Takes the request (room, bags, time) and logs it
Arrives on time, knocks and announces, counts the bags with the guest
Reminds the guest to check for items left behind
Checks the bill is settled before releasing the luggage
Counts again at the car, loads safely, says goodbye and records the departure

essays.stem: Explain how bell staff should lift and move luggage safely, and why this matters.
essays.modelAnswer: Bell staff lift many heavy bags each day, so poor lifting can cause back injuries that last a long time. Before lifting, I check the weight by tilting the bag and plan where it is going. I stand close to the load with my feet apart, bend my knees, keep my back straight and grip the bag firmly. I lift with my legs, keep the bag close to my body and do not twist; I turn my feet instead. If a bag is too heavy or awkward, I ask a colleague to help or use the trolley. I load the trolley with heavy cases at the bottom and do not stack it so high that I cannot see ahead. I push the trolley, rather than pull it, at a walking pace and take care on ramps, at doors and in lifts. Safe handling protects me from injury, protects the guest's belongings from damage and keeps other people safe from falling bags.
markingPoints: Checks the weight and plans the lift
Bent knees, straight back, load close, no twisting
Gets help or uses a trolley for heavy or awkward bags
Loads and pushes the trolley safely, with a clear view
Explains why: prevents injury and damage to belongings

essays.stem: Explain how bell staff help keep guests, their rooms and their belongings safe and secure.
essays.modelAnswer: Bell staff never say a guest's room number aloud and never tell a visitor which room a guest is in; instead they offer to call the guest from the desk. They never let anyone into a room, and send people who have lost a key to the front desk to prove who they are. Luggage is never left unattended in the lobby, corridors or at the entrance, and it is counted at every handover. Stored luggage is kept in a locked room and handed back only against the matching claim stub, or with ID checked as the procedure says. Guests are advised to keep valuables in the safe deposit box. Bell staff watch the entrance and lobby and report anything suspicious, such as an unattended bag or a person hanging around, to security at once without touching it. Found items go to lost property with a record. All jobs are written in the bell log, so that movements can be traced.
markingPoints: Room numbers kept private; visitors not given rooms or let in
Luggage never left unattended and counted at each handover
Locked storage, returned only against stub or checked ID
Reports suspicious bags or people to security without touching
Valuables advice, lost property recorded, jobs logged

essays.stem: A guest is moving from one room to another. Describe how you would move their luggage and belongings.
essays.modelAnswer: I get the room change slip from the front desk, showing the old and new rooms, and I collect the new key folder. I go to the old room with a trolley and, if the guest is there, I greet them and agree what is to be moved. If the guest is not there, I follow the property's rule, which usually means a supervisor or security officer goes with me and we list what we move. I pack nothing myself unless the guest has asked, and I move clothes on hangers as they are. I check the drawers, wardrobe, bathroom and safe so nothing is left behind; I never open the guest's safe myself. I take everything to the new room, place it neatly and check it with the guest. I return the old key to the desk, tell housekeeping the old room is empty, and record the move in the bell log with the time and my name.
markingPoints: Gets the room change slip and new key from the front desk
Moves with the guest present, or with a supervisor or security if not
Checks the old room so nothing is left; does not open the guest's safe
Places items neatly in the new room and checks with the guest
Returns the old key, informs housekeeping and records the move

essays.stem: Describe how bell staff deliver messages and parcels and run errands for guests, and why each job is recorded.
essays.modelAnswer: When a message comes in, it is written clearly with the date, time, the caller's name and number and the message, and the bell attendant delivers it to the room, or the desk turns on the message light. To deliver, I knock, announce "Bell service" and hand the message or parcel to the guest, checking their name. If there is a Do Not Disturb sign, I do not knock; I return the item to the desk and the guest is told another way, as the property's procedure says. For errands, such as posting letters or buying a newspaper, I fill in an errand card with the job, the room, the time I left and returned and any money handed over, and I give the guest the change and the receipt. Every job is recorded in the bell log or on the errand card so the bell captain knows where staff are, so jobs are not forgotten, and so there is proof if a guest asks later.
markingPoints: Messages written clearly with date, time, caller and message
Knocks, announces and hands over to the right guest
Respects Do Not Disturb and uses the property's other method
Errand card with job, times and money; gives change and receipt
Explains why records are kept: tracking staff, nothing forgotten, proof

essays.stem: Explain how a bell attendant should give guests information about local attractions and transport in Jamaica.
essays.modelAnswer: Guests often ask bell staff about places to visit, such as Dunn's River Falls, Rose Hall, the Blue Mountains, Negril's beach or the Bob Marley Museum, and about restaurants, shops and transport. I should know my area well, and keep the property's information folder, maps and leaflets up to date. I give clear, honest and polite answers, with directions, opening times and rough travel times if I know them. I never guess; if I am not sure, I say I will find out and come back, or I ask the concierge or tour desk. For transport, I suggest only licensed taxis and tour operators that the property approves, so the guest is safe, and I never take money from drivers for sending guests to them. I give safety tips politely, such as keeping valuables out of sight. Being friendly and well informed, as Team Jamaica training teaches, makes the guest's visit better and gives a good picture of Jamaica.
markingPoints: Knows local attractions and keeps information up to date
Gives clear, honest directions and times
Does not guess; checks or refers to the concierge or tour desk
Suggests only licensed, approved transport and takes no payments from drivers
Gives polite safety tips; friendly service in the spirit of Team Jamaica

essays.stem: A guest phones to say that one of her bags did not reach her room. Describe what you would do.
essays.modelAnswer: I apologise to the guest and stay calm and polite. I ask her to describe the bag: its size, colour, any name tag and what it contains, and I confirm her name and room quietly. I check the bell log to see how many bags were recorded at arrival and who delivered them. I search the likely places at once: the luggage room, the trolley, the bell desk, the lobby, the lift and the corridor, and I ask my colleagues. If it was a group arrival, I check whether it went to another room by mistake. I keep the guest informed, telling her what I am doing and when I will call back. If the bag is found, I deliver it, check it with her and apologise again. If it is not found quickly, I report it to my supervisor and security, and I check whether the bag ever arrived with her, for example with the airline. I record everything in the log.
markingPoints: Apologises, stays calm and gets a description of the bag
Checks the bell log for the count and who delivered
Searches the likely places and asks colleagues; checks other rooms for groups
Keeps the guest informed and delivers the bag if found
Reports to supervisor and security if not found, and records it

practical1.title: Arrival service and luggage storage with claim tags
practical1.brief: Set up a mock entrance and lobby at the Centre (a car, or a marked area as the car, a bell desk and a lockable room or cupboard as the luggage room). The assessor or other trainees play arriving guests, each with two to four pieces of luggage. Each member in turn: greets an arriving guest at the "car", helps them out, unloads and counts the luggage with the guest, checks for damage, loads the trolley correctly, takes the guest to the "desk", and then, because the room is not ready, stores the luggage with two-part claim tags and records it in the luggage storage log. Later, each member returns stored luggage to a different "guest" against the claim stub. The assessor will give one member a guest who has lost the stub. Members who are not working play guests or keep the log. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the completed log to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A car or a marked area as the car, a bell desk and a lockable luggage room or cupboard
A luggage trolley with a top rail
Suitcases, a garment bag and small bags (2–4 pieces per guest), one marked fragile
Two-part claim tags, luggage tags and pens
A luggage storage log or bell log
photos: Greeting the guest and helping them out at the car
Luggage counted with the guest, and any damage pointed out
Trolley loaded correctly: heavy at the bottom, garment bags on the rail
Claim tags on the bags and the stub given to the guest
Bags stored together in the locked luggage room
Luggage handed back against the matching stub
checklist: Greeted the guest promptly and politely at the car and helped them out
Checked nothing was left in the car
Counted the bags with the guest and pointed out any damage
Lifted safely and loaded the trolley correctly
Tagged the bags with two-part claim tags and filled in the log correctly
Stored the bags together in the locked luggage room
Handed bags back only against the matching stub, or followed the procedure for a lost stub
safety: Lift with bent knees and a straight back, keep loads close and get help with heavy bags
Do not overload the trolley; push it and keep it under control
Stay clear of moving vehicles; the car's engine must be off during the role play
Use only made-up guest names and details

practical2.title: Departure luggage service and errand delivery
practical2.brief: Use a mock guest room, a front desk, a bell desk and a mock entrance at the Centre. Part 1, departures: the assessor or another trainee "phones" the bell desk to ask for help with luggage. Each member in turn takes the call, logs it, goes to the room, knocks and announces, counts the bags with the guest, reminds the guest to check the room and safe, takes the luggage to the lobby, checks with the "desk" that the bill is settled, and loads the luggage into the "car" with the guest counting. Part 2, errands: the group receives three tasks from the desk (a written phone message, a parcel and a request to post letters). Each member completes at least one task: fills in an errand card, delivers the item correctly (one room will have a Do Not Disturb sign), and records it in the bell log. Members who are not working play guests or the desk agent. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, the errand cards and the bell log to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A mock guest room with a safe (or a box marked "safe") and a Do Not Disturb sign
A front desk, a bell desk with a phone and a mock entrance or car
A luggage trolley and 2–4 pieces of luggage per guest
Blank errand cards, a message pad and a bell log
A parcel, some letters and a written phone message
photos: The departure request written in the bell log
Knocking and announcing at the guest's door
Bags counted with the guest in the room
Checking with the desk that the bill is settled
Luggage loaded in the car, heavy cases at the bottom
Completed errand cards and the message slip
A parcel handed to the guest at the door
checklist: Took the departure call politely and recorded room, bags and time
Knocked, announced and greeted the guest at the room
Counted the bags and reminded the guest to check the room and safe
Checked the bill was settled before releasing the luggage
Loaded the car safely and counted the bags again with the guest
Filled in an errand card fully and correctly
Delivered the item to the right guest, and respected the Do Not Disturb sign
Recorded every job in the bell log
safety: Lift with bent knees and a straight back; get help with heavy bags
Load the car boot with heavy cases at the bottom and close it carefully, keeping fingers clear
Stay clear of moving vehicles; the car's engine must be off during the role play
Use only made-up guest names and details
